transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-08-21 16:00 PDT | Duration: 48m | Recording: yes
Attendees: Samira Patel (Redwood AE), Luca Moretti (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (Verdant Head of Eng), Derek O'Leary (Verdant CISO), Priya Raman (Verdant Platform)

00:00 Samira: hey everyone, thanks for joining, we are Samira from Redwood inference, with Luca our solutions engineer. quick agenda — security posture, deployment options (hosted/dedicated/private), and any compliance blockers.
00:12 Maya: hi, thanks. i think derek will lead the security bits, i'm mostly here for context on infra.
00:18 Derek: yea, thanks. our questions are pretty standard: SOC2, iso if you have it, how SSO works, scim, RBAC, audit logs, and importantly K M S integration and retention.
00:32 Luca: sounds good. to level set — Redwood offers hosted api, dedicated reserved pools, and a private vpc/on-prem option. all of the same API surface but differ on who holds keys and network isolation.
00:45 Derek: do you have a SOC 2 Type II? and iso 27001?
00:50 Samira: we do have SOC 2 Type II; ISO is in progress — current timeline end of Q4. i'll share the attestation and a redacted control matrix after this call.
01:02 Derek: and where's customer data stored for hosted? eu/na locations? residency controls?
01:07 Luca: hosted can be region pinned — we have na and eu regions today; data residency guarantees are part of enterprise contracts. persistence depends on request type — embeddings and logs are retained as configured, and you can request deletion per our retention controls.
01:25 Priya: for our compliance we need audit logs with immutable records and specific fields (user id, api key id, request id, model version, response hashes). can you provide schema?
01:35 Samira: yes, we can share example audit log schema. we also support streaming logs to customer S3 or SIEM via secure connectors for enterprise.
01:48 Derek: about KMS and encryption — do you offer BYOK? hsm? key wrap?
01:55 Luca: short answer: yes, BYOK is supported in Private deployments and Dedicated can be configured with customer-managed KMS on request. For hosted we offer envelope encryption with keys we manage, but enterprise hosted customers can use a managed BYOK arrangement via cloud KMS in some cases — we'll need legal and ops to finalize. we can support AWS KMS, GCP kms, and on-prem HSMs for private.
02:18 Maya: is key rotation supported and do you store plaintext anywhere?
02:22 Luca: keys rotate per provider policy; we don't persist plaintext model state or inputs outside of ephemeral memory used for inference. persisted logs and embeddings are encrypted at rest.
02:32 Derek: ok but we need a proof flow — show us how the key never leaves our control. sample flow would help.
02:37 Luca: absolutely, i'll put together a BYOK flow diagram showing envelope encryption, key wrapping, and where caches may hold KV cache — apologies, sometimes the transcript generator says kv cash — it's kv cache in the runtime.
02:52 Priya: on SSO — we use SAML2 with SCIM for user provisioning. how does redwood integrate?
02:57 Samira: we support SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning for enterprise accounts. you can map SAML attributes to roles, and SCIM props for groups. RBAC lives in our console — roles, routes, and API key scopes.
03:12 Derek: can we restrict token scopes to particular model versions or rate limits per team?
03:18 Luca: yes, token scoping is supported. you can scope keys to models, routes, and assign quotas. we also have per-token cost and latency tracking for observability.
03:29 Maya: about auditability — do you keep immutable logs for the admin actions like role changes and key rotations?
03:36 Samira: yes, admin audit logs are captured; log retention windows are configurable for enterprise and can be exported to customer-managed storage for long-term retention.
03:46 Derek: retention policy — default retention for request logs and embeddings?
03:50 Luca: defaults are 90 days for detailed request logs and 365 for billing/aggregates, embeddings retention is configurable; for Private you control retention entirely.
04:04 Derek: what about deletion guarantees — if we ask for deletion, is that immediate and auditable?
04:09 Samira: we support data deletion requests; we'll provide a deletion report showing objects removed. private deployments defer entirely to customer's controls.
04:18 Derek: legal will want to see an architecture diagram showing where data is decrypted for inference and where any outputs are stored.
04:24 Luca: i'll attach a runtime architecture diagram — it will show runtime nodes, KV cache behavior, where envelope decryption occurs (on the runtime node using ephemeral keys), and fallback policies.
04:36 Maya: on the hosted side, is the inference runtime multi-tenant? will other customers potentially share the same GPU?
04:42 Luca: hosted is multi-tenant at the runtime level but logically isolated. for strict isolation we recommend Dedicated or Private — Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools and stronger tenancy boundaries.
04:55 Derek: what are the SLA guarantees for dedicated vs hosted?
05:00 Samira: Dedicated has SLA-backed uptime and latency targets; hosted has best-effort SLOs for self-serve tiers but enterprise-hosted customers can negotiate SLAs in contract.
05:12 Priya: cross-region failover — how are keys and logs replicated?
05:18 Luca: replication depends on deployment. For hosted we replicate per-region per-customer settings; for Dedicated you can request geo-replication and for Private you control replication entirely. keys managed by customer’s KMS typically don't leave the KMS boundary.
05:31 Derek: any third-party pen tests or bug bounties?
05:35 Samira: yes, we run regular third-party penetration tests and have a bug-bounty program. i'll include the summary of the latest pentest in the packet.
05:45 Maya: about model artifacts — if we upload custom models, where are those stored and how are they encrypted?
05:52 Luca: customer model artifacts in Dedicated/Private are stored in customer buckets or in encrypted blobs with customer-managed keys depending on configuration. Hosted can accept customer models under enterprise agreements with customer-managed storage options.
06:10 Derek: compliance docs — can you provide example SOC2 controls mapping to our policy?
06:15 Samira: yes, i'll send a redacted control matrix mapping.
06:20 Derek: we need to know the granularity of audit logs: do you log prompt text and response text or do you only log metadata by default?
06:29 Luca: by default we log metadata; logging full prompts/outputs is optional and configurable — for high-sensitivity data we advise against storing full text and instead store hashes and ephemeral traces.
06:41 Priya: does Redwood offer field-level redaction or PII scrubbing before logs are written?
06:45 Luca: we can enable PII scrubbing pipelines and offer pre-log hooks for transforming or masking fields before persistence. integration examples will be in the security packet.
06:58 Derek: on RBAC — can we integrate with existing groups and map to permissions downstream?
07:03 Samira: yes, via SCIM and directory mapping you can tie groups to Redwood roles, and roles control API, console, and admin actions.
07:12 Maya: curious about rate limiting per-team — we have internal quotas and would like policy enforcement hooks.
07:17 Luca: you can set per-key quotas and alerts; for more complex policy enforcement we offer webhooks and integrations with our console and event streams.
07:29 Derek: do you have WORM-style logs or tamper-evident storage?
07:34 Luca: we support write-once export to S3 with immutability flags for audit scenarios; also signatures on exported logs can be provided.
07:44 Maya: curious about the runtime cache — you mentioned KV cache, is that persisted to disk? can that include customer data?
07:51 Luca: KV cache is an in-memory structure optimized for speed; some cache spill to local ephemeral SSDs depending on runtime config but those are encrypted and ephemeral. for strict controls choose Private where you control disk and lifecycle.
08:07 Derek: what about data ingress — do you allow direct VPC peering or private link?
08:11 Samira: we support VPC peering and private link options for enterprise; Private deployments can be fully inside your network.
08:19 Priya: how much instrumentation do we get for tracing requests?
08:23 Luca: per-request tracing is available, including per-token latency breakdowns, kernel selection traces, and model version info. traces can be pulled into your observability stack.
08:35 Derek: are there any known security limitations with streaming or function-calling that we should be aware of?
08:42 Luca: streaming is the same security model — but callbacks to third-party tools need to be firewalled; function-calls that hit external endpoints should be proxied or restricted. we'll show best-practice patterns.
08:55 Maya: for hosted, if we need guaranteed throughput spikes, can you guarantee burst capacity?
08:59 Samira: yes, we have burst capacity options and autoscale policies for Dedicated. hosted customers can also buy burst packages in enterprise plans.
09:09 Derek: retention again — for eDiscovery we may need 7 years for some logs. can you support extended retention?
09:15 Luca: yes, exports to customer-controlled storage allow arbitrary retention. we can also retain longer on our side per contract terms.
09:24 Samira: any blockers on your side for moving forward?
09:27 Derek: we need to validate the cape — sorry, validate the flow: BYOK for hosted is always the sticky point. we prefer keys never leaving our KMS.
09:36 Luca: understood, for hosted we'll propose a managed BYOK handshake where key material stays in customer KMS and we only receive wrapped keys; for absolute control Private is recommended.
09:46 Maya: timeline — we're targeting a pilot by Nov. what would you need?
09:51 Samira: we typically need a security NDA, SOC2 packet, architecture diagram, and a small POC scope. we'll also assign a solutions engineer for the deep-dive.
10:03 Derek: please send the SOC2 and pentest summary. also we'll prepare a list of required fields for audit logs.
10:10 Samira: noted. i'll add those to next steps.
10:15 Priya: one last Q — does Redwood offer contractual indemnities related to data breaches?
10:20 Samira: our enterprise contracts include standard indemnities; legal can iterate on specific clauses.
10:27 Derek: ok thanks, next i want a deeper session on KMS flow and runtime decryption boundary with your SEs.
10:33 Luca: happy to do that — we can include runtime folks and infra.
10:36 Samira: i'll coordinate times and share the packet.
10:40 Maya: thanks everyone.
10:42 Derek: thanks.

Post-meeting notes: action items and next steps reviewed. Samira to upload SOC2, pentest summary, and control matrix. Luca to prepare BYOK/KMS flow + IAM snippets and runtime diagram. Verdant to provide exact audit fields and retention windows.
